{{Quote|I will tolerate the Jedi presence in our ancestral home, ''if'' they surrender their weapons.|Ursa Wren|<ref name="LoM" />}}
The '''Wren Stronghold''' was the home of the renowned [[Mandalorian]] [[Clan Wren|Wren clan]], located on the frigid [[Planet|world]] of [[Krownest]]. A stunning complex built using [[steel]] and [[glass]], the large but minimalist stronghold was seen as a testament to the honor, adaptability, and design capabilities of the Mandalorian people. Constructed at the edge of a frozen lake, surrounded by [[tree]]s and [[mountain]]s, the stronghold blended into the surrounding snowy landscape. The ancestral home of Clan Wren, by the [[time]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Imperial Era|reign]], the stronghold was the seat of power for the [[Mandalorian clan|clan's]] [[Count|leader]], [[Ursa Wren]], protected by numerous [[Soldier|warriors]] and [[starfighter]]s.

==Description==
[[File:YouAreSoGrounded-SWRS03E16.jpg|thumb|left|275px|The Wren Stronghold's great hall]]
The Wren Stronghold was a large mansion<ref name="EpisodeGuide">{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/legacy-of-mandalore-episode-guide|text="Legacy of Mandalore" Episode Guide | Star Wars Rebels}}</ref> built on the [[planet]] [[Krownest]], a frigid world of ice and snow<ref name="Krownest">{{Databank|krownest|Krownest}}</ref> located within the borders of [[Mandalore sector|Mandalorian space]]<ref name="RebelsRecon">{{RebelsRecon|KPtdpmKvEwE|#3.16: Inside "Legacy of Mandalore" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/rebels-recon-inside-legacy-of-mandalore}}</ref> in [[the galaxy]]'s [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]].<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> Constructed from [[steel]] and [[glass]] to a minimalist aesthetic,<ref name="WrenStronghold">{{Databank|wren-stronghold|Wren Stronghold}}</ref> the stunning complex<ref name="Krownest" /> was situated along the edge of a frozen lake, amidst [[tree]]s and [[mountain]]s,<ref name="LoM" /> where it elegantly blended into the snowy landscape of Krownest as a testament to the adaptability and design capabilities of the [[Mandalorian]] people.<ref name="WrenStronghold" /> The stronghold was guarded by several members of [[Clan Wren]],<ref name="LoM" /> and a number of [[Fang-class Protectorate fighter|''Fang''-class starfighters]].<ref name="ZeroHour">{{Rebels|Zero Hour}}</ref>

Entrance to the Wren Stronghold was achieved via a flight of stairs on either end of the complex's lakeward face. Within, the stronghold housed communication facilities, as well as areas for members of Clan Wren to spar.<ref name="LoM" /> The complex also featured an expansive great hall,<ref name="EpisodeGuide" /> furnished with a long dining table and a large [[throne]] for the clan leader. The great hall was decorated with a number of [[chandelier]]s, wall-mounted light fixtures, several potted [[plant]]s, and a [[Painting|portrait]] of [[Portrait of Ursa Wren|the leader of Clan Wren]] displayed over the throne. Leading off from the great hall at the front of the complex was a small balcony that overlooked the nearby lake.<ref name="LoM" />

==History==
{{Quote|I'll take you to the stronghold, but I can't vouch for how you'll be greeted.|Tristan Wren, speaking to his sister Sabine upon her return to Krownest|<ref name="LoM" />}}
[[File:PresentForMom-SWRS03E16.jpg|thumb|right|275px|Ursa and Sabine Wren meet at the Wren Stronghold]]
The Wren Stronghold was the ancestral home of Clan Wren,<ref name="LoM" /> a legendary family of Mandalorian [[Soldier|warriors]].<ref name="ClanWren">{{Databank|clan-wren|Clan Wren}}</ref> During the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], the stronghold acted as the [[Mandalorian clan|clan's]] seat of power,<ref name="ZeroHour" /> and was the residence of the clan's [[Count|leader]], [[Ursa Wren]], her son [[Tristan Wren|Tristan]], and several other members of Clan Wren.<ref name="LoM" /> In the [[Standard year|year]] [[2 BBY]],<ref name="Legacy of Mandalore date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> Ursa's estranged daughter, [[Sabine Wren]], journeyed to the Wren Stronghold with a group of friends—including the [[Jedi]] [[Kanan Jarrus]] and [[Ezra Bridger]]—in an effort to recruit her clan to the growing rebellion against the Empire. Despite initial hostilities, Sabine and her allies were welcomed into the complex by Ursa Wren, though the Jedi were forced to relinquish their [[lightsaber]]s before entering the Mandalorians' home.<ref name="LoM" />

While Sabine attempted to negotiate an alliance with her [[Parent|mother]], even gifting her ownership of the [[Darksaber]]<ref name="LoM" />—a longstanding icon of Mandalorian authority she had recently [[Skirmish on Dathomir|reclaimed]] from the former [[Sith Lord]] [[Maul]]<ref name="TotD">{{Rebels|Trials of the Darksaber}}</ref>—Ursa chose to instead to offer the Jedi to the Empire in exchange for amnesty for both her daughter and Clan Wren, contacting the Imperial [[Viceroy]] of [[Mandalore]] in secret. Soon after, Viceroy [[Gar Saxon]] arrived at the Wren Stronghold with a cadre of [[Imperial Super Commando]]s, and it was there that the Empire's puppet ruler revealed his intentions to betray Ursa, and [[Death|kill]] Clan Wren along with the Jedi. [[Skirmish on Krownest|Fighting]] quickly broke out in the great hall between the Imperial-aligned super [[commando]]s and the forces of a Jedi-backed Clan Wren, eventually leading to the deaths of numerous super commandos, while Saxon and Sabine Wren engaged each other in a bout of [[Lightsaber combat|single combat]] that spilled out onto the nearby frozen lake. Sabine emerged victorious, though it was Ursa who ultimately killed Saxon, firing on the Imperial [[governor]] when he attempted to [[Blaster|shoot]] Sabine in the back after she chose to spare his life. Though the Jedi later departed Krownest, Sabine chose to remain with her clan at the Wren Stronghold, to continue the Mandalorians' fight against the Empire.<ref name="LoM" /> With the death of Gar Saxon, [[Mandalorian Civil War (Imperial Era)|civil war]] between Clans Wren and [[Clan Saxon|Saxon]] soon broke out.<ref name="ZeroHour" />

During the Empire's devastating [[Battle of Atollon|assault]] on the rebellion's [[Chopper Base|base of operations]] on [[Atollon]], Ezra Bridger returned to Krownest to once again ask Clan Wren for their aid against the Empire. At the Wren Stronghold, Bridger informed the Mandalorians of the Imperial attack, only to learn of the hostilities between Clan Wren and the Imperial-aligned Clan Saxon. Though their forces were spread thin, Ursa Wren chose to allow her daughter Sabine and a group of Wren volunteers to depart Krownest with Bridger in order to reinforce the besieged rebels on Atollon. The Mandalorian volunteers arrived in the [[Atollon system]] not long after, and it was due to their efforts the Imperial [[Interdictor]] vessel positioned over Atollon was ultimately destroyed, allowing numerous rebel ships and personnel to escape the planet and continue the fight against the Empire.<ref name="ZeroHour" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Wren Stronghold first appeared in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in "[[Legacy of Mandalore]]," the sixteenth episode of the animated ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' television series' [[Star Wars Rebels Season Three|third season]],<ref name="LoM" /> premiering [[February 18]], [[2017]].<ref name="Screener">{{WebCite|url=http://tvlistings.zap2it.com/tv/star-wars-rebels-legacy-of-mandalore/EP018796240072|text=Star Wars Rebels : ''Legacy of Mandalore''|date=2017-01-05|work=[http://tvlistings.zap2it.com Screener]|archivedate=20170121152406}}</ref>

The look of the Wren Stronghold in ''Star Wars Rebels'' was strongly influenced by the aesthetics of architect [[Wikipedia:Frank Loyd Wright|Frank Loyd Wright's]] [[Wikipedia:Prairie School|"Prairie" style of design]]. The portrait of Ursa Wren that hangs in the stronghold's great hall was rendered in a style similar to that of notable artist [[Wikipedia:Gustav Klimt|Gustav Klimt]].<ref name="EpisodeGuide" />
